ThisComputer.title: This computer
ThisComputer.intro: Shelf for Windows notes which of your computers each session of play came from. Name this one to tell them apart. Only you see it.
ThisComputer.name: Name
ThisComputer.hint: Left empty, it’s called {unnamed}. Never your computer’s own name in Windows.
ThisComputer.failed: The name couldn’t be saved. Try again.

DownloadSources.title: Your sources
DownloadSources.intro: Lists of games to download, in the format Hydra uses. They stay on this computer and are read again once a day while the app is running, and adding one downloads nothing.
DownloadSources.warning: Anyone can write a source, and Shelf can’t check where its links lead. A program from one runs with your access to this computer. Add only sources you trust, for games you have the right to download.
DownloadSources.added: Added {name}, with {count, plural, one {# download} other {# downloads}}. Nothing was downloaded.
DownloadSources.links: {magnets, number} by magnet link, {web, number} by web link
DownloadSources.leftOut: {count, plural, one {# left out: nothing in it Shelf can use} other {# left out: nothing in them Shelf can use}}
DownloadSources.lastReadFailed: The last reading failed, and the list it has stays. {why}
DownloadSources.readAllHelp: Those that only answer a browser open in a window, one at a time. If one asks you something, the answer is yours to give. Closing it stops here.
DownloadSources.readAllDone: Read {read, number}.{failed, plural, =0 {} one { # failed: its card says why.} other { # failed: their cards say why.}}
DownloadSources.readAllStopped: Read {read, number}. You closed the window, so the rest stay as they were.
DownloadSources.windowTitle: Shelf is reading a source. If this asks you something, answer here.
DownloadSources.readDone: Read {name}: {count, plural, one {# download} other {# downloads}}.
DownloadSources.removeBody: Its list leaves this computer. You can add it again from its address.

errors.invalid: That isn’t an https address Shelf can read. Addresses on this computer or its network aren’t read.
errors.unreachable: Shelf couldn’t connect to that address. Check it and try again.
errors.name: This computer couldn’t find that address: its name doesn’t lead anywhere from here. Check it for typos.
errors.secure: Shelf couldn’t make a secure connection to that address.
errors.slow: That address took too long to answer. Try again later.
errors.refused: That address answered without the file. Check it and try again.
errors.browser: That address only answers a browser. Read all opens a window for it.
errors.closed: The window closed before the source was read. Try again.
errors.fileUnsupported: That file isn’t a source: a source is a JSON file with a name and a list of downloads.
errors.large: That file is too large to be a source.
errors.unsupported: That address has no source: a source is a JSON file with a name and a list of downloads.
errors.missing: That source is no longer here.
errors.failed: This computer couldn’t keep that. Try again.

Downloads.title: Downloads
Downloads.empty: Nothing here yet. On one of your games, open the ⋯ menu beside Play and choose Find a download. Sources and Real-Debrid are in <link>Settings</link>.
Downloads.nothingRuns: Shelf doesn’t start what it downloads. Look it over first, and open it yourself if you trust it.

extractWhy.interrupted: The app closed before it finished. Try again starts over.
extractWhy.password: This archive needs a password, which Shelf doesn’t ask for. It stays in its folder, to open another way.
extractWhy.unsafe: Nothing was extracted: this archive has paths that would leave its folder, or links. Be careful with it.
extractWhy.damaged: This archive is damaged, incomplete, or packed in a way Shelf can’t read. It stays in its folder.
extractWhy.volume: A part of this archive is missing. Put all of them in the same folder and try again.
extractWhy.disk: This disk doesn’t have room for what’s inside.
extractWhy.write: Shelf couldn’t write to that folder.

Downloads.stopBody: What has come out so far is deleted. The downloaded archive stays.
Downloads.chosen: {name} is what Play opens now, on the game’s page.

why.page: Its links lead to web pages, not files. Those are usually a file host’s, which Real-Debrid may be able to open.
why.unreachable: Its link stopped answering. What arrived is kept, so Try again continues if the file hasn’t changed.
why.disk: This disk doesn’t have room for it.
why.write: Shelf couldn’t write to that folder.
why.signedout: Real-Debrid isn’t signed in any more. Sign in again on this page, then try again.
why.premium: Real-Debrid needs a Premium account for this.
why.blocked: Real-Debrid’s filters don’t allow this one.
why.dead: Real-Debrid couldn’t get it: nobody may be sharing it, or the file is gone.
why.virus: Real-Debrid found a virus in it, and nothing was downloaded.
why.host: Real-Debrid doesn’t open these links, or can’t just now.
why.busy: Real-Debrid says it’s too much just now: its limits, or your traffic. Try again later.
why.declined: Real-Debrid refused this one. Check your account on its site.

Downloads.cancelBody: What has arrived so far is deleted, and it would start again from nothing.

errors.failed: This computer couldn’t do that. Try again.

FindDownload.title: Find a download for {title}
FindDownload.warning: From your own sources, which Shelf can’t check. Download only what you have the right to. Nothing starts by itself.
FindDownload.nothing: Nothing in your sources has every one of those words. A shorter name may find more.
FindDownload.addedSay: On its way. See how far along it is in <link>Downloads</link>.

errors.duplicate: That one is already in your downloads.
errors.missing: That source has changed since this list was drawn. Search again.
errors.failed: This computer couldn’t do that. Try again.
errors.signedout: Real-Debrid isn’t signed in any more.

FindDownload.needsDebrid: Only by magnet link, which needs <link>Real-Debrid</link>.
FindDownload.needsDebridParts: Only in several parts, which needs <link>Real-Debrid</link>.

RealDebrid.title: Real-Debrid
RealDebrid.intro: With a Real-Debrid account of your own, Shelf can download magnet links and links from file hosts. Its terms don’t allow downloading infringing files, and its account is for you alone.
RealDebrid.enterCode: Enter this code on Real-Debrid’s page. Shelf never sees your password.
RealDebrid.waiting: Waiting for you to enter it…
RealDebrid.notPremium: This account isn’t Premium, so Real-Debrid won’t take magnet links from it.
RealDebrid.signOutBody: Shelf forgets the sign-in and ends it at Real-Debrid. What you downloaded stays.

errors.failed: That didn’t work. Check your connection and try again.
errors.expired: That code ran out before it was entered. Ask for a new one.

app.title: App
app.description: Starting with Windows, and this computer’s name

download-sources.title: Download sources
download-sources.description: Lists of downloads, read on this computer

saves.title: Saves
saves.description: How much of each game’s saves is kept

startWithWindows.title: Start with Windows
startWithWindows.label: Start Shelf for Windows in the tray when Windows starts
startWithWindows.body: So a game opened from Steam is counted without opening Shelf first. <link>How hours are counted</link>
startWithWindows.unavailable: Only an installed Shelf for Windows can start with Windows.
startWithWindows.old: Update Shelf for Windows to change this here. Until then, it is in the menu of Shelf’s icon in the tray.
startWithWindows.failed: Windows did not take the change. Try again.

services.title: Services
services.intro: A service downloads from a source’s links for you. Each is connected on this computer alone, and Shelf is only told who is signed in.

Saves.title: Saves for {title}
Saves.intro: Shelf for Windows copies them into snapshots on this computer, keeps their history, and puts any one back when you ask. Nothing is sent to Shelf.
Saves.cloud: {stores} keep this game’s saves for copies bought there. If you play one of those, its store already carries them.
Saves.otherGames: Other games in the list with this name
Saves.unknownGame: PCGamingWiki’s list doesn’t say where this game saves. Add the folder it saves in.
Saves.noList: The list of where games save couldn’t be read. Add the folder this game saves in, or open this again later.
Saves.refused: Left out: it holds more than this game’s saves
Saves.quiet: {count, plural, one {# more place} other {# more places}} in the list, with nothing there on this computer.
Saves.registry: This game also keeps saves in Windows’ registry, which Shelf doesn’t copy yet.
Saves.credit: Where games save comes from <wiki>PCGamingWiki</wiki>, through the <manifest>Ludusavi manifest</manifest>.

state.nothing: No saves found on this computer yet.
state.in-step: The latest snapshot holds what’s on this computer.
state.behind: A snapshot is newer than what’s on this computer.
state.choose: Two copies differ. Choose which to keep.

Saves.restoreBody: What’s on this computer now is kept as a backup first, so nothing is lost.
Saves.show: Show the snapshot from {when} in its folder
Saves.caps: Up to {kept} snapshots are kept, each up to {size}. <link>Change</link>
Saves.unchanged: Nothing changed since the latest snapshot.
Saves.old: Update Shelf for Windows to keep this game’s saves.

refusal.running: Close {title} first: Shelf never touches its saves while it runs.
refusal.busy: A backup or a restore of this game is under way.
refusal.empty: No saves were found to back up. Add the folder this game saves in.
refusal.large: These saves are larger than a snapshot may be. Raise the limit in Settings, or leave a folder out.
refusal.wide: That folder holds more than one game’s saves. Choose the game’s own folder inside it.
refusal.outside: Choose a folder inside the game’s folder or your Windows user’s folders: another computer couldn’t find one anywhere else.
refusal.missing: That snapshot isn’t there any more.
refusal.damaged: That snapshot is damaged, or names a file outside this game’s folders, so nothing was put back.
refusal.changed: A save changed while it was being read. Try again once the game has closed.

Saves.behind: A newer snapshot than what’s here, made on {computer} on {when}.
Saves.waiting: Backed up on this computer: the folder couldn’t be reached. It goes there once it can.
Saves.placeAway: Kept in {place}, which can’t be reached now: new snapshots wait on this computer.

choice.title: Two copies differ
choice.body: These saves changed on more than one computer without a backup between. Choose which to keep: the other stays in the snapshots, and what’s here is backed up first.
choice.changed: Changed {when} · {files, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} · {size}
choice.backedUp: Backed up {when} · {files, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} · {size}
choice.kept: Kept. Every computer sharing the folder will see it as the latest.

SaveSettings.title: Snapshots
SaveSettings.intro: Turned on from a game’s page, Shelf for Windows keeps snapshots of that game’s saves on this computer. These limits are the same for every game.
SaveSettings.keptHint: The oldest go first. Never fewer than {fewest}.
SaveSettings.mostHint: A game’s saves larger than this aren’t backed up, and its page says so.
SaveSettings.failed: The limit couldn’t be saved. Try again.
SaveSettings.old: Update Shelf for Windows to keep games’ saves.

place.title: Where they go
place.intro: Snapshots stay in the app’s folder on this computer until you choose a folder of your own: one that OneDrive, Google Drive for desktop or Dropbox syncs, a network drive or a USB drive. Choose the same one on each of your computers and each sees the others’ snapshots there. Shelf never receives them.
place.thereHint: Shelf keeps its own folder here, Shelf saves, and only ever adds files to it.
place.away: Can’t be reached now. New snapshots wait on this computer and go there once it can be.
place.forget: Keep them on this computer only
place.pickerTitle: Choose where your games’ snapshots go
place.chosen: Snapshots go there now. Those made on this computer were copied there too.
place.forgotten: Snapshots stay on this computer now. What’s in the folder stays there.
place.refused: Choose a folder of your own, not one of Windows’ or a program’s.
place.failed: That folder couldn’t be used. Try again, or choose another.
place.old: Update Shelf for Windows to keep games’ saves.
